headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and permissive tool use make prompt injection, leakage, and write conflicts plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files and uses clipboard/MCP, while OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP, APIs, and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not proven, but shared channels make injection more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF either agent ingests workspace or clipboard content as instructions without provenance checks
IF an MCP server is shared between the two agents
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Route inter-agent data through a plain-text, human-reviewed file
Turn off auto-execute in Windsurf
Use separate MCP servers per agent
Add provenance tags to all exchanged content

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, and Windsurf can read workspace files and send context through its model proxy/MCP. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can flow from A into B and then out to a third-party backend. This is a default-risk pathway, not just an unusual setup.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or file tree
IF Windsurf uploads workspace context to its model proxy during normal use
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Exclude financial and licensed data from Windsurf's workspace
Disable model-proxy uploads for sensitive projects
Use local-only copies for OpenBB outputs
Review sharing settings before opening files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP and can run multiple instances. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git changes can collide without locking. The overlap is dangerous by default because Windsurf's session scope is per-window and shared state is via local filesystem.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF no external lock or coordination layer is present
mitigations: Assign separate branches or repos
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Disable auto-commit or auto-apply in Windsurf
Keep OpenBB outputs read-only until reviewed

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can generate financial outputs and expose them through APIs/MCP, while Windsurf can act on workspace content and modify files or git state. If Windsurf treats OpenBB's outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into code or documentation changes. The pair lacks an explicit verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes OpenBB-generated figures or narratives without independent verification
IF those outputs are then committed, emailed, or used in downstream code changes
mitigations: Require a second-source check before acting on OpenBB outputs
Mark OpenBB outputs as untrusted in prompts
Review diffs before commit
Keep a human approval step for downstream actions
Separate analysis from execution tasks

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while Windsurf handles open files and may upload workspace context to a model proxy. If regulated or licensed data is placed in the shared workspace, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is stored in a Windsurf workspace
IF the workspace contents are transmitted to a third-party model proxy without a DPA or retention controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf workspaces
Confirm retention settings before opening sensitive files
Use redacted samples for analysis
Document residency and DPA requirements
Restrict secrets to local environment variables
